claims.text: The magnetocaloric response and hysteresis of as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type HEAs arise from nanoscale chemical and lattice inhomogeneities.
Nanoscale chemical and lattice inhomogeneities locally modulate magnetic exchange interactions.
Nanoscale chemical and lattice inhomogeneities create local variations in the magnetostructural transition temperature.
These inhomogeneities produce a narrow, hysteretic transition in the as-deposited state.
Homogenizing short-range chemical order broadens the distribution of local transition temperatures and reduces hysteresis.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type alloy has a single-phase hexagonal structure.
The as-deposited alloy contains nanoscale regions with subtle chemical ordering and associated local strain.
Annealing at approximately 600–700 °C for several hours can promote diffusion and homogenize local chemical order.
The proposed annealing process can homogenize local chemical order without changing the overall hexagonal phase.
An inert annealing atmosphere will prevent oxidation.
Local chemical ordering and lattice-strain variations mediate local differences in magnetic exchange and magnetostructural transition temperature.
The as-deposited alloy undergoes a strongly first-order magnetostructural transition with a large magnetocaloric response.
Annealing-induced homogenization can alter the overall magnetocaloric performance of an HEA.
Annealed samples should have a broader magnetic-entropy-change profile than the as-deposited baseline.
Annealed samples should have less hysteresis during low-applied-field magnetization cycles than the as-deposited baseline.
Annealing may slightly lower the peak magnetic entropy change.
A broader entropy-change profile and lower hysteresis would improve reversibility and cycling performance in magnetic refrigeration.
The predictions are limited to low-applied-field cycling near room temperature while the hexagonal phase is retained.
Processing that destabilizes the hexagonal phase or substantially changes composition may fall outside the predicted behavior.
Failure to observe systematic entropy-peak broadening and reduced hysteresis after annealing is proposed as a falsifying result.

contradictions.description: Chemical and strain heterogeneity is said to generate local transition-temperature variations, yet it is also said to produce a narrow transition, while reducing those variations by homogenization is predicted to broaden the transition. The direction of the proposed distribution-width effect is internally inconsistent unless an additional broadening mechanism is specified.
